text: Maschke's theorem shows that for a finite group $G$ with $\mathrm{char}(k)\nmid|G|$ the group algebra $k[G]$ is a ___ ring, so Artin-Wedderburn expresses it as a product of matrix algebras.
explanation: Complete reducibility of every module is exactly the statement that $k[G]$ is a semisimple ring; Artin-Wedderburn then gives $k[G]\cong\prod_i M_{n_i}(D_i)$. Over $\mathbb{C}$ each division ring $D_i=\mathbb{C}$, yielding $\mathbb{C}[G]\cong\prod_i M_{n_i}(\mathbb{C})$ with $\sum_i n_i^2=|G|$.
